sections.h2: Which office handles Crawford County deeds?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds Office at 200 W. Michigan Avenue in Grayling takes every deed for land in the county. Crawford County is among the 31 Michigan counties that merge the clerk's job with the register's, and the register's line is (989) 348-2841.

Walk-ins are welcome without an appointment, weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30, with a closure for lunch between 12:00 and 1:00. The counter takes cash, checks, money orders and cards, and cards add a service charge.

Mail works too. Send the document, a return envelope with postage, and a check or money order made out to Crawford County or Crawford County ROD.

Three vendors handle e-recording here: CSC, Indecomm and Simplifile. Only Simplifile can submit a paper that needs the treasurer's certification, so a home sale deed usually goes through that one. Ask your title company or closing attorney which vendor they use before you plan around e-recording, and allow time for the treasurer's certificate to be issued first.

One flat $30 covers any document, however many pages. The fee schedule has been in force since October 1, 2016 under Public Acts 224 through 232 of 2016, and $4 of each fee feeds the state's survey and remonumentation fund.

Crawford County register charges that often show up in a house sale
ServiceAmount
Recording, any document$30.00
Extra instrument on a release or assignment$3.00 apiece
Treasurer's certification before a warranty deed is recorded$5.00
Certifying a recorded copy$5.00
Paper copies$1.00 a page
Tapestry online search$8.95 each name or legal description

Fold the $5 certification into the same payment as the recording fee. The treasurer does not need a second check.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax calculated for a Crawford County sale?
sections.html:
Divide the price into $500 slices, round a partial slice up, and multiply: $3.75 per slice for the state, 55 cents per slice for the county. MCL 207.504 backs the county figure for counties under 2,000,000 people.

  • The seller carries the bill, and the stamps must be bought in Crawford County itself.
  • Land that straddles a county line needs the price allocated between the counties, with each one taxed on its share.
  • Show the full consideration on the deed, or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, which costs nothing to file.
  • Write any exemption into the deed. Examples: value under $100, foreclosure transfers, and quitclaims that merely repair a title defect.

Michigan's state act, MCL 207.526, also exempts gifts to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild. The county act's list holds no such item, so ask Grayling how the county portion is handled.

sections.h2: When the Crawford County Treasurer has to certify a deed
sections.html:
Four kinds of paper need it: warranty deeds, other deeds that include a warranty covenant, land contracts, and land contract assignments with warranty wording. MCL 211.135 tells the register to hold such papers until the certificate arrives.

The treasurer sits at the same address, 200 W. Michigan Ave, on the same weekday schedule, and answers at (989) 344-3231. The certificate reports liens and tax titles and confirms five years of paid taxes. Quitclaims lacking warranty covenants are exempt.

Delinquent taxes can be paid online, by text-to-pay, with digital wallets, by ACH or on autopay, all with fees. Request a payoff figure first, then choose the closing date.

sections.h2: How a Crawford County home sale reaches the register
sections.html:
Start with the deed. Your closing attorney or title company prepares it, and you sign where a notary can acknowledge it. If it carries warranty wording, the Crawford County Treasurer certifies the taxes next. Ask for a payoff figure early so any delinquent balance is cleared from your proceeds rather than found at the last minute.

Then comes payment. The closing agent buys the transfer tax stamps in Crawford County and writes one check for the recording fee and the $5 certification. The package goes to Grayling in person, by mail with a prepaid return envelope, or through Simplifile.

After recording, the deed gets a liber number and an image goes into the files. Watch for the return of the original and keep it with your closing papers. If you sold for cash to a buyer with no lender, the steps are the same minus the mortgage paperwork, which is why these sales can close quickly when the taxes are already paid.

sections.h2: Crawford County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Land ownership shapes this market. Of roughly 360,000 acres, over three quarters belong to the State of Michigan, the U.S. Forest Service or the Department of Military Affairs. The county has six townships and one city, Grayling, which is its only incorporated community.

About 13,722 people live here, and only 23.3 live on each square mile. Owners occupy 79.6% of occupied homes, rent is $862 at the median, the median household income is $60,392, and builders took out 27 permits in 2025. Rural and wooded parcels are common, so be ready to describe water, septic and internet service at the property when a buyer asks.

Sign up for the register's free alert service. It sends an email or phone notice when a document is filed under your name, which is the fastest way to learn that someone has recorded a bogus deed against your property.

The office's files reach back to 1879. It keeps an image of each document rather than the original deed, which is stamped with a liber number after recording. Visitors can search on public computers at the counter, and Tapestry (occasional users) and Laredo (subscribers) offer remote search.

Staff will not draft documents or answer legal questions. They point owners toward a real property attorney, a title company, or a blank deed from an office supply store, with a warning that forms found online might not satisfy Michigan's format rules.

Before the deed travels to Grayling, run through these points with your closing agent.

  • Does the deed warrant title? If so, order the treasurer's certification.
  • Who buys the transfer tax stamps, and for what amount?
  • Does the legal description copy the previous deed, and does the deed name its drafter with an address?
  • Are delinquent taxes outstanding, and will proceeds clear them?
  • Is the transfer paperwork headed to the local assessor, along with a rescission of any principal residence exemption effective on closing day?

Rural parcels raise extra questions about wells, septic systems and private roads. Those belong with the county's health and road authorities, because the register of deeds only deals with the recorded paper.

faqs.q: What does it cost to file a Crawford County deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars flat. A warranty deed also needs the treasurer's $5 certification, and a release that names several instruments adds $3 for each additional one.

faqs.q: What transfer tax rates apply in Crawford County?
faqs.a: The seller pays $3.75 to the state and 55 cents to the county for each $500 slice of price, with stamps bought in Crawford County itself.

faqs.q: Does the Grayling register close for lunch?
faqs.a: Yes, daily from 12:00 to 1:00. Otherwise the counter serves walk-ins on weekdays until 4:30, no appointment needed.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in Crawford County?
faqs.a: Yes, through CSC, Indecomm or Simplifile. Simplifile is the one the county names for papers needing tax certification.

faqs.q: Is a tax certificate needed for a quitclaim?
faqs.a: Not when the quitclaim has no warranty covenants. Warranty deeds and land contracts do need it under MCL 211.135.
